verdict.rationale: NVIDIA's docs publish 96 GB of GDDR7 memory and say the card can run AI locally, with an FP8 Transformer Engine for LLM inference. That capacity is plausibly enough for a quantized 70B-class model, and a community four-card build reports 41k tok/s of inference throughput. However, no memory-bandwidth figure is published; the only bandwidth claim is for PCIe Gen 5. A critic also notes that SM120 lacks support in the main libraries, which focus on SM100. missing for 10: published GPU memory bandwidth spec, explicit 70B-class quantized model guidance or benchmarks, independent single-card 70B inference results.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run a 70B-class quantized LLM on this GPU — published VRAM capacity and memory bandwidth that make local or single-node inference practical

citations.quote: With 96 GB of memory on the RTX PRO 6000, you can turn your desktop into an AI powerhouse for fine-tuning LLMs, generative AI, and running autonomous AI agents locally and securely.
equipped with 96 GB of ultra-fast GDDR7 memory
A second-generation FP8 Transformer Engine—shared with data center-class NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs—accelerates LLM prototyping, inference, and AI development
After the fix they got back to 41k tok/s.
